# EnterpriseGlue v0.35.9 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.35.8`.

## Highlights

- **mission-control:** Returns generic not-found responses for missing runtime process instances without changing tenant or runtime authorization.

## User and administrator impact

- Completed or unknown process IDs queried through an authorized engine no longer become internal errors on runtime instance endpoints.

## API and integration compatibility

- Runtime process-instance authorization and read handlers classify only typed engine.read HTTP404 as generic NOT_FOUND.
- Historic process-instance handling shares the same classification; other typed errors retain their identity and unknown errors remain sanitized.
- Documents all nine runtime instance-read paths at explicit tenant and tenant-host compatibility URLs, including required engine selectors, authentication and typed error envelopes.

## Database migrations

- No schema or persisted-data changes.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- Authentication, engine tenancy, runtime-resource permissions and private engine transport remain mandatory.
- Unknown errors and upstream response bodies are not disclosed; upstream authorization or availability failures are not classified as not found.

## Documentation

- docs/development/testing-engine-tenancy-and-access-control.md

## Known limitations

- A published image remains immutable; deployments require a newly qualified forward release.

## Rollback

- Revert the application image; there are no data changes to undo.

## Validation evidence

- Both production and modular routers cover engine-wide and resource-aware missing IDs, concurrent removal between guard and handler, foreign engine denial, typed upstream failures and lookalikes.
- Protected candidate, current exact-image security, database portability and post-upgrade API denial acceptance remain required.
